faq.q: What is the origin of Zayd?
faq.a: Zayd is associated with Arabic. Zayd is Arabic زَيْد (Zayd), meaning 'growth, increase'. It was borne by a companion of the Prophet.
Yes — the underlying form زَيْد is Arabic.
Zayd can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Zayd should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Zayd is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Zayd, zayd. Script forms are زيد, زَيْد, زید, ज़ैद.

faq.q: Is Zayd a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
